mainTopic: שבת נא: — The end of במה טומנין (insulating food, cold food, melting ice) and the start of במה בהמה: which gear an animal may wear on שבת, and whether extra security is a משאוי
overview: This amud finishes the chapter במה טומנין and opens a new chapter. First, the ברייתא ends its rules on insulating food: a pot may not be removed and put back, fine flax chaff counts like manure, and vessels may be stacked or sealed with dough only to keep heat in, never to add it. The תנא קמא forbids insulating cold food, while רבי permits it. Crushing snow or hail into water on שבת is forbidden, but letting it melt by itself in a cup is fine. After the הדרן, a new משנה asks what gear an animal may wear into the public domain on שבת, pairing each animal with its normal control device. The גמרא defines the unusual terms and then asks whether an animal may wear stronger gear than it needs. After a proof is pushed off, the גמרא shows this is a dispute between תנאים about a cat with a collar, and rules like חנניה: extra security is not a משאוי. The amud ends with a story about לוי and רבה בר רב הונא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: He may not remove the pot and put it back
steps.stepSummary: The closing clause of the ברייתא from the previous page: in the case being discussed, one may not take the insulated pot out and return it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may not take the pot out and then put it back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a sentence of the ברייתא that started on the previous page. It rules that in that case, a person may not lift out the insulated pot and put it back in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new topic. It is the last line of a rule about a pot that is already insulated. When the pot is fully covered with something that may not be moved on שבת, there is nothing to take hold of it by, so the ברייתא forbids taking it out and putting it back (רש״י on the previous amud).

keyTerms.meaning: Insulating food to keep its temperature

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a sentence from the previous page. It is not a brand-new rule standing alone. If it feels like it starts in the middle, that is because it does.

phrases.english: He may not remove [the pot] and return it.
phrases.notes: This finishes the ברייתא's case that started on the previous page.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In that case, one may not remove the insulated pot and return it.

steps.title: Fine flax chaff is like manure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rules that fine flax chaff counts as a material that adds heat, just like זבל (manure).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the chaff of fine flax is like manure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a new material to the list of things that are forbidden for insulating. He says fine flax chaff works like manure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Manure is one of the classic materials that מוסיף הבל, meaning it actively adds heat. One may not insulate in such materials even before שבת, because of the worry that a person will come to stir hot coals. רבי יהודה says fine flax chaff also generates heat, so it belongs in that forbidden group.

keyTerms.meaning: Chaff, the waste fibers shaken loose from flax
Manure, a material that gives off heat
Adds heat, the category of materials forbidden for insulating

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the deciding question is how a material behaves, not its name. Anything that actually produces heat falls into the forbidden category.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
the chaff of fine flax
is like manure.
phrases.notes: So one may not insulate in it, even on ערב שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A Tanna's added opinion within the same ברייתא, classifying a material.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fine flax chaff has the status of manure, a heat-adding material that may not be used for insulating.

steps.title: Which vessels may be stacked on which
steps.stepSummary: One may place a copper urn on a copper urn, or a clay pot on a clay pot. One may not mix them, putting a pot on an urn or an urn on a pot.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may place a copper urn on top of another copper urn, and a clay pot on top of another clay pot. But one may not place a clay pot on top of a copper urn, or a copper urn on top of a clay pot.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a new practical case: stacking hot vessels on שבת. It allows stacking same on same and forbids mixing the two kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the two vessels are the same kind, the bottom one does not really heat the top one, so stacking only keeps heat in. When the kinds are mixed, there is a concern that the top vessel will actually be heated by the bottom one. That would be adding heat on שבת, which is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A copper urn, usually for heating water

phrases.english: One may place an urn on top of an urn
and a pot on top of a pot,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֹא קְדֵרָה עַל גַּבֵּי מֵיחַם,
phrases.english: but not a pot on top of an urn,
or an urn on top of a pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case within the same ברייתא, moving from insulating materials to stacking vessels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stacking is allowed when both vessels are the same kind and forbidden when the kinds are mixed.

steps.title: Sealing a pot with dough, only to keep heat in
steps.stepSummary: One may seal a pot's mouth with dough. All these permitted actions are allowed only to preserve heat, not to add heat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may seal its mouth with dough. All this is not in order to heat it up, but only so that its heat will be kept in.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא allows sealing the pot's opening with dough. It then states the guiding principle behind all the permitted cases: you may keep heat in, but you may not make the food hotter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This purpose clause sums up the whole topic. Any act whose goal is to heat the food is forbidden on שבת. An act that only guards existing warmth from escaping is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: The key line is: keeping heat in (שיהיו משומרים) is permitted, but adding heat (שיחמו) is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, preserving versus adding heat, is the backbone of the whole סוגיא of טמינה.

phrases.english: And he may seal its mouth with dough,
and not in order that they become heated,
but only so that they will be preserved [keep their heat].
phrases.notes: Applies to all the cases above.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more permitted act, then gives the reason behind all the permitted acts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sealing with dough is permitted, and all such acts are permitted only to preserve heat, never to add it.

steps.title: Cold food may not be insulated either
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says that just as hot food may not be insulated, cold food may not be insulated either.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as one may not insulate hot food, so too one may not insulate cold food.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now asks about the opposite case: wrapping cold food to keep it cold. The first opinion forbids it, just like insulating hot food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Insulating cold food does not add heat, so it might seem obviously allowed. The תנא קמא still forbids it, treating any insulating the same way so that people do not confuse the cases. This sets up the next step, where רבי disagrees.

keyTerms.meaning: Insulate, wrap up to keep the temperature

phrases.english: And just as one may not insulate hot [food],
so too one may not insulate cold [food].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question within the ברייתא: does the ban on insulating extend to cold food?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא holds that insulating cold food is forbidden, just like insulating hot food.

steps.title: רבי permits insulating cold food
steps.stepSummary: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) disagrees and permits insulating cold food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי permitted insulating cold food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי disagrees with the opinion just stated and allows wrapping cold food. This dispute is what the גמרא will go on to discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, the ban on insulating was made because of hot food, out of concern about adding heat. With cold food that concern does not apply, so there is no reason to forbid it.
steps.confusionAlert: Plain 'רבי' with no name is רבי יהודה הנשיא. He is a different person from the רבי יהודה (בר אילעאי) who spoke in step 2.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא forbids insulating cold food, while רבי permits it.

phrases.english: Rabbi permitted insulating cold [food].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion to the תנא קמא of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, insulating cold food is permitted.

steps.title: No crushing snow or hail on שבת, but letting it melt in a cup is fine
steps.stepSummary: Crushing snow or hail so it turns into water is forbidden on שבת. Putting it in a cup or bowl to melt on its own is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: On שבת you may not crush snow or hail to make its water flow out. But you may put it into a cup or a bowl, and you do not need to worry.
steps.whatsHappening: The text gives one more שבת rule before the chapter ends. You may not actively crush ice into water, but you may let it melt by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushing the ice actively makes a new thing, water, out of solid ice. This is like creating something new on שבת (מוֹלִיד), so it is forbidden. Putting it in a cup is passive: the ice melts by itself and the person does nothing, so there is no concern.

keyTerms.meaning: Crushing or breaking up (here, ice into water)
So that its water will flow out
And he need not worry (it is fully permitted)

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not the melting itself. The problem is a person actively crushing the ice to produce water. Ice melting by itself in a cup is completely fine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is a basic source in הלכה for the difference between actively making a liquid on שבת and letting it form on its own. The difference matters for ice cubes and similar cases.

phrases.english: And one may not crush

phrases.aramaic: לֹא אֶת הַשֶּׁלֶג וְלֹא אֶת הַבָּרָד
phrases.english: neither the snow nor the hail
on Shabbat so that its water will flow out,
but he may place it into the cup
phrases.notes: The word אֲבָל marks the shift from forbidden to permitted.

phrases.english: or into the bowl, and he need not worry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מְרַזְּקִין לֹא אֶת הַשֶּׁלֶג וְלֹא אֶת הַבָּרָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list of שבת rules, moving from insulating food to melting ice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Actively crushing snow or hail to produce water is forbidden on שבת. Placing it in a vessel to melt by itself is permitted.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter במה טומנין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the chapter במה טומנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter במה טומנין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line formally closes the chapter about insulating food on שבת. The next line starts a brand-new chapter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן means 'we will return to you'. It is a traditional farewell said at the end of every chapter, expressing a wish to come back and learn it again. It adds no new law.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (chapter-closing formula)
'With what may one insulate': the name of the chapter just finished

steps.whatToRemember: The chapter במה טומנין taught what you may and may not use to keep food warm on שבת, and that you may only preserve heat, not add it.

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'With what may one insulate'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that ended with step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter on insulating food on שבת is complete.

steps.title: New chapter opens: what may an animal go out wearing?
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens by asking which items an animal may wear into the public domain on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: With what may an animal go out on שבת, and with what may it not go out?
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a heading question. It sets up the list of rules that comes right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person must let his animals rest on שבת, so an animal may not carry a load into the public domain. The question is which items count as part of the animal's normal gear, which is allowed, and which count as a load, which is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the start of a new משנה)

steps.confusionAlert: This chapter is not about a person carrying. It is about the animal 'carrying'. The rule comes from the duty to let one's animal rest on שבת.

phrases.english: MISHNA: With what may an animal go out
and with what may it not go out?

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמֶּה בְּהֵמָה יוֹצְאָה וּבַמָּה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new chapter and a new topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Some items may be worn by an animal in the public domain on שבת and some may not. The details follow.

steps.title: Four animals and the control gear each may wear
steps.stepSummary: Four animals are listed, each paired with the gear it normally uses to be led or controlled. Each may go out wearing that gear.
steps.simpleTranslation: A camel may go out with an אפסר (halter). A נאקה (a type of camel) may go out with a חטם (nose ring). Libyan donkeys may go out with a פרומביא (bridle). A horse may go out with a שיר (neck chain).
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts answering its question by listing specific animals and the gear each one may wear. The גמרא will define these unusual words later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item is the normal tool for controlling that kind of animal. Because it is the animal's proper guarding gear, it counts as part of the animal and not as a load. The pairings are specific: each animal gets only the gear that suits it.

keyTerms.meaning: Halter (a head rope used to lead an animal)
A type of camel (defined in the גמרא)
A nose ring for leading the animal
Libyan donkeys / a bridle or muzzle-type control

steps.confusionAlert: Each gear is allowed only for its own animal. Do not assume any animal may wear any of these items.

phrases.english: A camel may go out with a halter,
and a naka with a nose ring,
phrases.notes: The גמרא will explain what a נאקה is.

phrases.english: and Libyan donkeys with a perumbiya (bridle),
and a horse with a neck chain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first specific answers to the heading question in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each animal may go out on שבת with the gear that is normally used to control it: camel with a halter, נאקה with a nose ring, Libyan donkeys with a bridle, horse with a chain.

steps.title: General rule: animals that normally wear a chain may go out with it
steps.stepSummary: Any animal that normally wears a chain may go out with the chain and may be led by it.
steps.simpleTranslation: All animals that normally wear a chain may go out wearing the chain and may be pulled by the chain.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה widens the horse case into a general rule for every animal that usually wears a chain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה adds two things. First, the permission covers every animal that normally wears a chain, not only horses. Second, it allows not just wearing the chain but actively leading the animal by it. Since leading is the chain's real job, it stays guarding gear and does not become a load.

keyTerms.meaning: A chain or ring worn around an animal's neck
Animals that normally wear a chain

steps.whatToRemember: An animal may go out on שבת with gear that is normal for controlling it. That gear counts as part of the animal, not as a load. Animals that usually wear a chain may both wear it and be led by it.

phrases.english: And all animals that wear a chain
may go out with a chain and be pulled by the chain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the horse-with-chain case from step 10 into a general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every animal that normally wears a chain may go out with it on שבת and may be led by it.

steps.title: The chains can be purified while still on the animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by teaching that an animal's chain that became טמא can be sprinkled and immersed without removing it from the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we sprinkle purifying water on them, and immerse them in their place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one last detail about the animal chains from the previous line. It says they can be purified while the animal is still wearing them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These chains are real objects that can become טמא. The משנה says you may sprinkle מי חטאת on them and do טבילה right where they are, without taking them off the animal. This is a טומאה detail attached to the שבת list, and the גמרא will discuss it later.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkle purifying water (מי חטאת) to remove טומאת מת
Immerse them in a מקוה to purify them
In their place, meaning while still on the animal

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not about carrying on שבת. It is a separate טומאה law about the same chains, added at the end of the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה ends here: each animal may go out with its own normal gear, and a chain can be purified while still on the animal.

phrases.english: And we sprinkle [purifying water] on them,
phrases.notes: Refers to the chains from the previous line

phrases.english: and immerse them in their place.
phrases.notes: Without removing them from the animal

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a purity law about the same chains mentioned in step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal's chain may be sprinkled and immersed for purification while it is still on the animal.

steps.title: The גמרא asks what 'a female camel with a nose device' means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה's phrase נאקה בחטם refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is 'a נאקה with a חטם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the meaning of an unclear phrase from the משנה. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words נאקה and חטם are not obvious, so the גמרא wants to know exactly which animal and which device are meant. To know what is allowed, we first have to know what the משנה is describing.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of the discussion on the משנה

phrases.english: What is 'a naka with a ḥatam'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא by clarifying a term from the משנה listed in step 10

steps.title: A white female camel with an iron nose ring
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה explains that נאקה בחטם means a white female camel with an iron nose ring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: A white female camel with an iron nose ring.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה answers the question. נאקה is a white female camel, and חטם is an iron nose ring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This narrows the case. It is not just any camel, but a white female camel. That kind of camel needs the stronger control of a nose ring, so for her the nose ring counts as her normal gear and not as a burden.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
A white female camel
with an iron nose ring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נאקה בחטם means a white female camel with an iron nose ring.

steps.title: A Libyan donkey with an iron halter
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that לובדקים בפרומביא means a Libyan donkey with an iron halter.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'לובדקים with a פרומביא': רב הונא said: A Libyan donkey with an iron halter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defines a second unclear term from the משנה in the same way. רב הונא says it means a Libyan donkey with an iron halter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'what does it mean?' is understood here without being repeated. A Libyan donkey is strong and hard to control, so an iron halter is its normal gear.

keyTerms.meaning: A Libyan donkey, known as a strong, high-quality breed

phrases.english: And 'luvdekim with a perumbiya' —
phrases.notes: The question 'what is it?' is implied

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
A Libyan donkey
with an iron halter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same define-the-term pattern as steps 13 and 14 for a second term
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לובדקים בפרומביא means a Libyan donkey with an iron halter.

steps.title: Levi tries to buy a Libyan donkey and gets barley instead
steps.stepSummary: Because a Libyan donkey was just mentioned, the גמרא tells a story: לוי sent money to buy one, and the people sent back barley to teach that a donkey's strength comes from its food.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי sent money to בי חוזאי to buy him a Libyan donkey. They tied up [the money], and sent him barley, to say that a donkey's strides depend on barley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes a short side trip with a story connected to the Libyan donkey. It is not a new הלכה about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי thought he needed a special breed. The people of בי חוזאי returned his money and sent barley instead. Their message was that if you feed an ordinary donkey well, it will walk as well as a Libyan donkey.

keyTerms.meaning: A place name, the region of Ḥozai
Strides, the way an animal walks

phrases.english: Levi sent money
to Bei Ḥozai
to buy him a Libyan donkey.
They tied up [the money and returned it] and sent him barley,
to say that a donkey's strides depend on barley.
phrases.notes: Good food makes a good donkey

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side story connected by the mention of the Libyan donkey in step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A donkey's quality depends on its feed more than on its breed.

steps.title: May one animal go out with another animal's gear?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, reports that students asked רבי about switching gear between animals, such as a camel wearing another animal's device.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: They switched [the cases] before רבי and asked: what is the law for this [animal] with that [animal's gear]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to halacha with a new question about switching gear between animals. This question sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה paired each animal with its own gear. Now the question is whether an animal may go out wearing a device meant for a different animal. If that device is not normal for this animal, it might count as a burden (משאוי). Or perhaps it is still allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: That of this one on that one, meaning one animal's gear on another animal
What is [the law]? An open question

steps.whyThisMatters: This question leads into the idea of extra security: whether a stronger device than the animal needs counts as a forbidden burden.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They switched [the cases] before Rabbi,
What is [the law of] this one with that one's [gear]?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַחְלִיפִין לִפְנֵי רַבִּי, שֶׁל זוֹ בָּזוֹ מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side story and goes back to the משנה's pairings, asking about swapping them
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an animal may go out on שבת wearing gear meant for a different animal, or whether that counts as a burden

steps.title: The easy case: a white female camel in a halter is clearly not allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says there is no question about a נאקה in an אפסר. The halter cannot control her, so it is a משאוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: You don't need to ask about a white female camel in a halter. Since a halter doesn't control her, it is a burden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is narrowing the question the students asked רבי. It first sets aside an easy case so it can point to the real doubt in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת an animal may wear gear that guards it, but gear that does not guard it counts as a load it is carrying. A strong נאקה is not controlled by a light אפסר, so the halter is just a משאוי. This case is too weak, so it is obviously forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A halter or bit, a light device for leading an animal
"You should ask", meaning this is the case worth asking about
A burden or load, which an animal may not carry on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: The rule is not "a stronger device is worse." Gear that is too weak is a burden because it does not do its job. The open question is only about gear that is stronger than needed.

phrases.english: A white female camel with a halter, you need not ask about,
since she is not controlled by it,
it is a burden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the students' question from step 17 by removing the obvious case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gear that cannot control the animal is a משאוי and is forbidden.

steps.title: The real question: a regular camel in a nose ring
steps.stepSummary: The real doubt is a regular camel wearing a strong nose ring when a halter would be enough. Is extra control a burden or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where you should ask is a camel with a nose ring. What is the law? Since a halter is enough for it, is the nose ring a burden? Or maybe we don't call extra security a burden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the real question. Is gear that gives more control than needed considered a burden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two sides. One side says that since the camel only needs a halter, anything stronger is unnecessary and therefore a משאוי. The other side says that extra security is still security, so it is not a burden.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)

steps.whyThisMatters: This question about נטירותא יתירתא drives the rest of the section. The proofs and the dispute between תנאים that follow are all about it.

phrases.english: Where you should ask is
a camel with a nose ring, what is the law?
Since a halter is enough for it,
is it a burden,
or perhaps, with extra security,
we do not say it is a burden?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ גָּמָל בַּחֲטָם מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After removing the easy case in step 18, this states the real question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether extra, unneeded security gear (a nose ring on a regular camel) counts as a משאוי on שבת.

steps.title: A proof from the list of four animals that go out with a halter
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי quotes his father: four animals go out with a halter, including the camel. The גמרא suggests the list means to exclude a camel in a nose ring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said before רבי: My father said that four animals go out with a halter: the horse, the mule, the camel, and the donkey. What does this come to exclude? Isn't it to exclude a camel with a nose ring?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone answers the question by quoting a teaching. The גמרא then tries to read from it that a camel may not go out with a nose ring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list says the camel goes out with a halter. The גמרא assumes the list is there to exclude something, and the natural candidate is a camel in a nose ring. If so, extra security would count as a משאוי.

keyTerms.meaning: What does it come to exclude?
Is it not? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְפָנָיו רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said before him:
So said my father:
Four animals go out with a halter:
the horse, the mule, the camel, and the donkey.
What does this come to exclude?
Is it not to exclude a camel with a nose ring!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי? לַָאו לְמַעוֹטֵי גָּמָל בַּחֲטָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to resolve the question from step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That a camel may not go out with a nose ring, because extra security counts as a משאוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's teaching, quoted by his son, that four animals including the camel go out with an אפסר.

steps.title: Pushing off the proof: the list excludes a white female camel in a halter
steps.stepSummary: The list does not exclude a camel in a nose ring. It excludes a נאקה in a halter.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It comes to exclude a white female camel with a halter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The list may be excluding something else entirely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list may be saying "a camel goes out with a halter, but a נאקה does not," since a halter cannot control a נאקה (step 18). Read that way, the list says nothing about extra security, so this proof fails. The גמרא then finds a dispute between תנאים (steps 23–26) and rules on it in step 27.

phrases.english: No, it comes to exclude a white female camel with a halter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only this proof. It does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The list may be excluding a different case, the נאקה in a halter, rather than a camel in a nose ring.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a Libyan donkey and a camel go out with a halter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a לובדקים and a camel may go out with an אפסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: A Libyan donkey and a camel go out with a halter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another ברייתא that allows a Libyan donkey and a camel to go out with a halter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This tells us these two strong animals are controlled by a light halter, so for them it is real guarding gear. It does not by itself say what happens if they wear something stronger. The next step brings a dispute between תנאים that addresses that question.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
A Libyan donkey and a camel go out with a halter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another source on which animals go out with a halter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Libyan donkey and a camel may go out on שבת with a halter.

steps.title: The question is a dispute between תנאים about a wild animal with a collar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the question matches a dispute between תנאים. The תנא קמא says a חיה may not go out with a סוגר. חנניה says it may, with anything that guards it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute between תנאים: A wild animal may not go out with a collar. חנניה says: It may go out with a collar, and with anything that guards it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the extra-security question was already argued about by תנאים. It quotes their dispute and will next work out what case it is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion forbids a collar, and חנניה allows any guarding device. For now it is unclear whether they are really arguing about extra security. The next steps check that.

keyTerms.meaning: A collar, a strong neck device for holding an animal

phrases.english: It is like a dispute between tannaim:
A wild animal may not go out with a collar;
Chananya says: It may go out with a collar
and with anything that guards it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from looking for a proof to showing that the question was a dispute between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא forbids a חיה to go out with a סוגר. חנניה allows a סוגר and any guarding device.

steps.title: What animal is the dispute about? Not a large wild animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the dispute is about. It cannot be a large חיה, because a collar is not enough to control it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say a large wild animal, is a collar enough for it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of animal the dispute is about. It rules out the first option: a big wild animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A collar cannot hold a large wild animal. For that animal the collar would be a משאוי according to everyone, and חנניה would not allow it. So the dispute cannot be about a large animal.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing?
If you say with a large wild animal,
is a collar enough for it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to define the case of the dispute in step 23 and rules out the first option.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of animal the dispute between the תנא קמא and חנניה is about.

steps.title: Not a small wild animal either
steps.stepSummary: If the case is a small חיה, a collar is clearly enough for it. Then why would the תנא קמא forbid it?
steps.simpleTranslation: But rather, a small wild animal? Isn't a collar enough for it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option, a small wild animal, and finds a problem with it too. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a small wild animal a collar works properly, so it is real guarding gear. Then the תנא קמא has no reason to forbid it. Both options fail, so the גמרא will need a third case where the two opinions really differ.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather (moves to the other option)

steps.whyThisMatters: Ruling out both simple options pushes the גמרא to find a case where a collar is more than needed. That case would show the תנאים really argue about נטירותא יתירתא.

phrases.english: But rather with a small wild animal,
is a collar not enough for it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out a large animal in step 24, this rules out a small animal too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the תנא קמא that a חיה may not go out with a סוגר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A collar fully controls a small wild animal, so it is real guarding gear and not a burden. There is no reason to forbid it.

steps.title: The dispute is about a cat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the תנאים argue about a cat. The תנא קמא holds that a collar is a burden because a simple cord is enough for a cat. חנניה holds that extra guarding is never a burden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case they argue about must be a cat. The תנא קמא holds: since a simple cord is enough for a cat, a collar is extra, so it counts as a burden. חנניה holds: any extra guarding is not called a burden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the puzzle from the last two steps. The argument is about a cat, an animal for which a collar is more than it needs, because a simple cord is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A large חיה needs more than a collar, and a small one is clearly fine with a collar. So neither fits the dispute. A cat is different: a thin cord is enough for it, so the real question is whether a stronger collar is 'too much'. The תנא קמא says more than needed counts as carrying a משאוי. חנניה says extra protection still counts as guarding the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a difference between them; this is the case they argue about
A mere cord, a simple string
A burden, a load that is forbidden to carry out on שבת
Extra guarding, more security than needed

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute is about a cat. Does guarding that is more than needed count as a burden? The תנא קמא says yes. חנניה says no.
steps.confusionAlert: Neither side says a collar is forbidden in general. The only question is whether a collar is too much for an animal that only needs a cord.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that a cat is the difference between them?
The first Tanna holds:
since a mere cord is enough for it,
phrases.notes: A cat can be controlled with a thin string.

phrases.english: it (the collar) is a burden;
and Chananya holds:
for any extra guarding,
we do not say it is a burden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty in step 25 by finding a middle case where the dispute makes sense.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: an animal (a cat) for which a mere cord suffices, so a collar is extra security
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute seemed impossible, since a large חיה is not held by a collar and a small one obviously is.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about a cat. The question is whether extra guarding beyond a cord counts as a משאוי.

steps.title: The הלכה follows חנניה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא quotes שמואל: the הלכה follows חנניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is like חנניה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: we follow חנניה. Extra guarding is not considered a burden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, an animal may go out on שבת with guarding that is stronger than it strictly needs. Since the dispute was shown to be exactly the question of step 19, this ruling also settles that question: extra security, such as a nose ring on a regular camel, is not a משאוי.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...

steps.whatToRemember: Final ruling: the הלכה is like חנניה. An animal may go out with extra guarding, and it does not count as a משאוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling settles the practical law. The story that follows involves the son of רב הונא בר חייא, the very person who reported this ruling.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chiya said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha is in accordance with Chananya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two opinions explained in step 26.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows חנניה: extra guarding on an animal is not a משאוי.

steps.title: Two scholars travel and one donkey goes ahead
steps.stepSummary: לוי, the son of רב הונא בר חייא, and רבה בר רב הונא were traveling together. לוי's donkey walked ahead of רבה's donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי, son of רב הונא בר חייא, and רבה בר רב הונא were traveling on the road. לוי's donkey went ahead of רבה בר רב הונא's donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story, so this step sets the scene. Two scholars are riding together, and one donkey moves in front.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Walking in front was a sign of honor, usually given to the greater scholar. רבה בר רב הונא was the greater scholar. So when לוי's donkey went first, even on its own, it looked like a lack of respect.

phrases.aramaic: לֵוִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא
phrases.english: Levi, son of Rav Huna bar Chiya,
and Rabba bar Rav Huna
were traveling on the road.
Levi's donkey went ahead
of the donkey of Rabba bar Rav Huna.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵוִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא הֲווֹ קָאָזְלִי בְּאוֹרְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a story about the son of רב הונא בר חייא, who reported the ruling in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative setup: לוי's donkey went ahead of the donkey of רבה בר רב הונא.

steps.title: רבה is offended and לוי plans to speak
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא felt hurt. לוי decided to say something to him so that... (the sentence continues on the next amud).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא was upset. לוי said to himself: I will say something to him so that...
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: רבה feels slighted, and לוי decides to calm him. This step sets up לוי's next words, which come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה thought לוי was going first to show he considered himself the greater scholar. לוי wants to fix the hurt feelings by saying something, and the purpose clause is cut off here. Most likely he will raise a Torah point that shows respect for רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A word, a matter (here, a Torah point)

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is cut off at כִּי הֵיכִי ('so that'). Its ending is on the next amud, so do not look for it here.

phrases.aramaic: חֲלַשׁ דַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna was offended.
Levi said: I will say something to him,
so that...

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲלַשׁ דַּעְתֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: the reaction to the donkey going first, and לוי's plan to respond.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative: רבה was offended, and לוי resolves to say something to him (continued on the next amud).
